# Storyboard: Chapter 4, The Glittering Scale

*Generated by `tools/storyboard.mjs` from `app/story/ch04.js`. Do not edit by hand: change the story file and run `node tools/storyboard.mjs` again.*

## How to read this

Every screen of the game is one comic panel, called a frame. Frames are listed in reading order. Each one has:

- **Shot**: the storyboard, written for an illustrator (camera, who is where, what the moment feels like, where the lettering goes).
- **Scene**: what the game draws today, in plain words: the set, the camera, who is in shot and how, and any effects.
- **Captions**: the narration boxes, read first. **Balloons**: who speaks, in order. **Sound effect**: the big lettering. A line marked *(only if …)* shows only to a reader whose choices match.
- **Then**: what the reader does next (tap Next, choose, type, pick a look, count by twos, or do a Counts lesson).

Where the reader makes a choice, each option’s frames are grouped under a **Branch** heading, and the branches meet again at the frame named after them. `{name}` is the first part of her Clan name (Moon makes Moonpaw), `{petname}` is what her Tall One calls her, and `{they}`/`{them}`/`{their}` become she/her/her or he/him/his. `{Murmur}`/`{murmur}` is the tortoiseshell’s name word: Murmur (Murmurpaw, Murmurchime, murmuring), or Mutter for a reader whose own Clan name is Murmur.

### f019 · panel 19

**Shot.** WIDE, FROM THE FRONT, THEN THE COUNTS. The prey pile laid out Tallyheart’s way under the bramble arch: two long rows of ten in the morning light, and a third at the back that is only a dark band in the brambles’ shadow, with nothing in it to make out. **Then the Counts lesson** `ch04-pile` (pieces, prey in rows): 3 × 10 (prey in rows in a thought cloud; its own question, and another of its own on its retry; its own lines after a right answer; its own lines after a right retry), 2 × 10 (lit a row at a time as it is asked; its own question, and another of its own on its retry; a check: a right one never makes the fact hard). She types each answer on the keypad; a miss gets the count scratched in the earth, and comes back two questions later (the questions in between come from `ch04-tens`, the easiest first, never a pair asked already while there is another, each asked in that lesson’s picture and words after “One from this morning.”). On to f020.

## The Case File’s cards

A piece of bark for each thing she finds out: one picture scratched in, one line, and a mark in a corner (an eye for what she saw herself, an ear for what she was only told). Each goes into her Case File at the panel that gives it, in this order:

| Card | Mark | Its line | Given at | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `four-a-night` | eye | Four gone every night. | f062 |  |
| `tidy` | eye | The thief leaves the pile tidy. | f063 |  |
| `dug-earth` | eye | Freshly dug earth behind the pile. | f063 |  |
| `scale` | eye | The ‘scale’ is smooth, like glass. | f063 |  |
| `fox-flew` | ear | The fox says it FLEW. | f066 | answered by `cant-fly` (for chapter 10); drawn touching them once ch4CaughtFly or ch7Flew is true: “They can’t both be true.” |
| `fox-moon` | ear | The fox says the MOON was out on the storm night. | f067 |  |
| `squall-shapes` | ear | Squall says two skinny shapes carry something to the tracks. | f087a | her file shows it only once foundSquall is true |
| `sprinkle-scales` | eye | Sprinkle’s scales are grey and bumpy. | f098 |  |
| `cant-fly` | eye | Sprinkle can’t fly. | f115 |  |

## The book page

Title: *{name}paw’s First Moon*. This chapter’s page, under “Chapter 4: The Glittering Scale”. Lines shown when their condition matches the reader’s choices:

- (always) On {name}paw’s third morning, the pile lay in rows of ten, and a gap showed in a heartbeat: four more pieces gone, twelve in three nights.
- (always) Tallyheart taught {name}paw {their} fourth Count, both forepaws, and scratched a fourth claw mark on the tree.
- (always) In the gap lay a glittering ‘scale,’ smooth, like glass.
- (always) A smiling fox named Reynard came to the border and said he saw a dragon fly off with the prey by moonlight. Most of the Clan believed him.
- (always) {name}paw asked a fair question, and Glintstar gave the dragon until the full moon.
- (always) {name}paw started a Case File: a piece of bark for every clue, with an eye for what {they} saw and an ear for what {they} was told.
- (if ch4CaughtFly is true) {They} caught one hole in the fox’s story: Reynard said the dragon flew, and Sprinkle can’t fly.
- (if foundSquall is true and ch5Roof is false or not set and ch9Roof is false or not set and not (ch4CaughtFly is true)) On the roof of {their} old tower, {they} found Squall, the littlest dragonet, who roars at airplanes and hiccups.
- (if foundSquall is true and ch5Roof is false or not set and ch9Roof is false or not set and not (ch4CaughtFly is true)) Squall told {them} about two skinny shapes that go to the tracks every night. A thing to check.
- (if foundSquall is true and ch5Roof is false or not set and ch9Roof is false or not set and ch4CaughtFly is true) On the roof of {their} old tower, {they} found Squall, the littlest dragonet, who told {them} about two skinny shapes that go to the tracks every night.
- (if foundSquall is false or not set) On the roof of {their} old tower, Sprinkle’s littlest brother is still roaring, and hiccuping.
- (if ch5Roof is true) On the roof of {their} old tower, Sprinkle’s littlest brother is still roaring, and hiccuping.
- (if ch9Roof is true and ch5Roof is false or not set) On the roof of {their} old tower, Sprinkle’s littlest brother is still roaring, and hiccuping.
- (always) Under the Old Bridge, Sprinkle looked herself over and said the scale wasn’t hers, and three friends made a thirty-claw promise.
- (always) That night there were forty in the rows, a moon as thin as a curl of bark, and a grey tom who fell asleep by fifty.
- (no dream typed) {name}paw’s dream that night is not in the Case File.

**A dragonet page:** Squall (`squall`), found in this chapter by a reader whose foundSquall is true (the page is there only then). Her book gains a page for Squall, with room for her own drawing, beside the clutch still to find (silhouettes, seven dragonets in all):

> The littlest of the clutch, slate grey with yellow flecks like sparks, and the loudest.
>
> {name}paw found him on the roof of the tallest tower, hugging the pole of the red light and roaring at airplanes.
>
> He thinks they are giant dragons.
>
> His roar ends in a hiccup. Five more claws, counted.
